Top-level 'references'/'n_bikes_swept'/'clusters'/'overall' keep the reports/acc_final_2026_08_08.json shape and use the epoch headline: round-2 labels, epoch binding + epoch source weights, every row scored under its own timing convention (1-ft rollout or first motion). 'headline' carries (a) that metric, (b) legacy rules on the same labels and (c) the EXACT published 2026-08-08 metric (HEAD 0bd0ea2 labels, legacy binding + weights). Trap in km/h (sim - published; sim = instantaneous finish speed, 'trap66' = 66-ft strip-trap average), 60 ft in s.

reference_fit.objective: minimax: min over (mu_peak_scale, launch_rpm_factor) inside the physical bounds of max_i |ET_i - pub_i| / tol_i (tol = tests/test_validation.py bands); within REF_FLAT of the optimum the most neutral point wins; the winner must keep all three references mass-monotone (-20..+20 kg)

notes.summary: Round-2 retune from NEUTRAL inside physical bounds (mu_peak_scale 0.95-1.15; launch_rpm_factor None or 0.45-0.75 x redline, 0.025 steps; 2T None only) with the joint objective w|d|_ET + 0.01 s/(km/h) x w|d|_trap, grouped 5-fold CV over benchmark rows, the one-standard-error rule toward the simplest family and a HARD mass-monotonicity gate (every catalog bike of a cluster ET(-10 kg) <= ET(0) <= ET(+10 kg), zero tolerance). Every row is scored under its own timing convention. Result: ZERO mass inversions (references -20..+20 kg and all 538 catalog bikes; scripts/check_mass_monotonicity.py exit 0), no litre bike traction-limited above 2nd gear, trap bias +2.87 km/h (published metric) vs +13.83 and top speed mean|d| 12.9 vs 28.1 km/h — but ET w|d| on the published metric is 0.3427 s vs 0.2629 (+0.080), i.e. the ET acceptance criterion is NOT met, and the K5 stays 0.04 s under its band.

acceptance_narrative.et: FAIL: (c) published metric 0.3427 vs 0.2629 (+0.0798); (a) epoch headline 0.3259; (b) legacy rules on new labels 0.3310. Not within +0.005.
acceptance_narrative.trap: PASS: weighted trap bias +3.19 (a) / +2.87 (c) km/h vs +13.83; +1.87 (a) on the 66-ft strip-trap convention.
acceptance_narrative.topspeed: PASS: mean|d| 12.9 km/h (83 matched) vs 28.1; bias +7.0.
acceptance_narrative.mass: PASS: 0 catalog inversions, references monotone (K5 +0.103..+0.114 s per 10 kg).
acceptance_narrative.references: K5 9.8309 (band 9.87-10.07: FAIL by 0.039 s), R1 10.1592 (pass), Hayabusa 10.4461 (pass); K5 60 ft 1.724 s with the 1-ft rollout (band 1.8-2.1 predates rollout timing) / 1.998 s from first motion (inside).
acceptance_narrative.clusters: entry-200-300 +0.265 and single-300-500 -0.265 are beyond +-0.25 (both neutral: no knob beats neutral by 1 SE). Shown data-limited: on rows with weight >= 0.5 their biases are +0.184 (n=7) and -0.145 (n=9); the excess comes from DERIVED 0-100 x 1.6 rows (Classic 350 family -4.2..-5.0 s, Pulsar/FZ25/CB300F +1.4..+1.8 s) and the category-default primary-ratio defect the data agent documented (298 bikes; small bikes geared too tall -> slow).

why_et_is_not_reachable_with_these_knobs: Neutral round-2 physics is 0.32 s FAST on average (bias -0.320, w|d| 0.454 on (a)); round-2 physics alone moved the neutral bias -0.149 -> -0.295 (hyb_neutral: round-2 physics + round-1 data) — the cooler tyre heat balance and the drag pitch moment add rear grip, and the combined-CoG launch is a PERFECT wheelie-limited launch (1st gear 60-80 % of steps on the wheelie ceiling, ~1.1 g) that no test rider reproduces.
The fast bias is concentrated in the high-power clusters: neutral litre-sport-195+ -0.54, litre-sport-600-1000 -0.45, sport-twin -0.40, other -0.16 s.

Grip cannot slow a wheelie-limited launch (grip profile flat above 1.0) and is bounded at 0.95 below; the CV puts it ON the lower bound in every cluster that uses it (litre-600-1000, sport-twin, other, reference) — the bound is binding, so the data wants more slowing than the bounds allow.

The only launch-slowing lever, the clutch-dump rpm as a FRACTION OF REDLINE, slows bikes very unevenly because their torque below ~0.5 x redline differs: tuned - neutral ET on litre-sport-195+ ranges -0.08 s (ZX-10R 2011) to +1.80 s (Ninja H2: the supercharger makes little boost at 6.6k), +1.43 (ZX-10RR), +1.28 (ZX-10R 2021), +1.05 (H2 SX) — sd 0.46 s around a +0.47 s mean. Centering the bias therefore costs spread: litre-sport-195+ ends at bias -0.02 but w|d| 0.45 (HEAD 0.147).

Top end: trap +4.4 / +3.4 / +3.4 km/h (litre-195+ / litre-600-1000 / sport-twin) on the instantaneous finish speed, +2.6 / +1.9 / +2.2 on the 66-ft strip trap — a residual ~1-2 % speed (3-6 % power-to-drag) excess on high-power bikes that no allowed knob addresses (the launch knob is compensating part of it).

decomposition_summary.metric: published metric (c): HEAD 0.2629 -> round-1 physics+data neutral 0.3829 (+0.120) -> round-2 physics (round-1 data) 0.4821 (+0.099) -> round-2 data 0.4655 (-0.017) -> round-2 retune 0.3427 (-0.123). Net +0.080.
decomposition_summary.labels_binding_timing: on a fixed model the switch from (c) to the epoch headline (a) is -0.003 (HEAD model) / -0.017 (tuned model); per-row timing vs a uniform 1-ft rollout is -0.0027 on the tuned model.
decomposition_summary.round1_for_comparison: the rejected round-1 knobs score 0.2738 on (c) (the verifier's apples-to-apples number) and 0.2631 on (a); round-1's own report figure 0.2627 is (a)-with-round-1-labels at a uniform 1-ft rollout and is reproduced exactly by this script (m_r1_tuned_ownlabels).

selected_knobs.litre_sport_195p: mu 1.05, launch 0.475 x redline — gate-CONSTRAINED: every unconstrained family left the BMW HP4 Race inverted (neutral: -10 kg slower by 5.3 ms = 2nd-gear wheelie threshold on a 215 hp / 146 kg bike; mu 0.95 also traction-limits it in 2nd -> +10 kg faster). CV + 1-SE over the 6 gate-feasible grid points (all launch 0.45-0.475). Cost vs the unconstrained choice (0.95, 0.525): (a) +0.014 s; that choice also had a litre bike traction-limited 7.9 % of gear>=3 steps.

notes.launch_rpm_justification: Cycle World, 'Launch at the dragstrip like a pro' (2014-08-13, https://cycleworld.com/2014/08/13/launch-at-the-dragstrip-like-a-pro): 'Bring the engine up to peak torque—usually between 4500 and 9000 rpm', 'Control your traction and speed with the clutch until the first upshift'. The selected 0.45-0.50 x redline is 5.9-7.0k rpm on 13-14k litre I4s and ~5.5k on an 11.5k Ducati V2 — inside that window. Electronic launch controls hold higher (0.55-0.75), which the bounds also allowed; the CV did not pick them.

physics_follow_ups: A launch-technique model that is uniform across torque curves: launch rpm relative to the torque curve (e.g. the rpm where torque first reaches X % of peak) instead of a fraction of redline, or a rider wheelie-margin fraction of the wheelie ceiling — either would slow the perfect wheelie-limited launch without the per-bike cliff (H2 +1.8 s) and stays mass-monotone.
Find the ~0.15 s neutral-bias shift of the round-2 physics (hyb_neutral vs r1_neutral) item by item (tyre heat balance, drag pitch moment, combined CoG, rollout geometry).
High-power top-end excess (+2-4 km/h trap on litre bikes even on the 66-ft convention).
Data: the category-default primary ratios (298 bikes) bias the small-bike clusters slow.
